Then there are cities where the rats are so numerous and so brazen that they work out private disputes by brawling midday on a train platform, or they lounge on your front porch, eating fallen fruit. New York City’s Flaco, the beloved Eurasian eagle-owl sprung from a cage in the Central Park Zoo, was found to have high levels of this kind of poison in his system when he died. It is not the only city to try the approach: Chicago is having luck with rat birth control in Wicker Park; Boston had mixed results in Jamaica Plain. Sign up for it here. If Democrats win control of the House in November, they will face a dilemma: Should they attempt a record third impeachment of Donald Trump? The president and his allies have warned that this would be a Democratic majority’s first move. “I’m going to be impeached. They’re going to impeach me,” Trump said last month at a rally in South Carolina. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has been noncommittal. “We haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out in terms of impeachment,” the would-be speaker told ABC’s This Week on Sunday. But Representative Jamie Raskin, the lead manager of Trump’s second impeachment, seemed more open. Earlier this month, on Meet the Press , he said that Trump had “undoubtedly” committed impeachable offenses. “We understand it’s not a panacea. It is a tool in the toolbox,” he said. “We will not hesitate to use it if we need to use it.” Realistically, House Democrats may have a hard time resisting impeachment. Their voters are in a punchy mood. manifest.title: ‘The Best Thing That Happened to Him Was Losing in 2020’
manifest.summaryEvidence: Few reporters understand as much about Donald Trump’s thinking, motives, and behavior as Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan. Haberman has been covering the president closely for more than a decade at The New York Times ; she started with his first campaign in 2015, and her record of scoops quickly brought her into the public eye. Swan was, for many years, her chief professional rival: He worked for Axios , where he landed a controversial 2018 one-on-one interview with Trump . In late 2022, the Times announced that it was hiring Swan, turning the rivals into colleagues. This past June, they published Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump . The book, an instant best seller, advances a new understanding of the first year of Trump’s second term, relaying in minute-by-minute detail how, since retaking office, he has pursued his personal goals with few limits on his power. The Atlantic staff writer Tim Alberta sat down with both authors at The Atlantic Festival, where he asked them about the 2028 election and the future of the presidency and the Republican Party.
